key_insight: Geometric locality lets Hamiltonian simulation be done with nearly optimal nearest-neighbor circuit depth, achieving an upper bound of O(T log(nT/ε)) and a matching lower bound up to a doubly logarithmic factor.
engineering_relevance: This sharpens the expected depth cost of simulating lattice quantum dynamics, guiding the design of scalable quantum compilers and hardware-aware simulation routines.
method: Use a Lieb–Robinson decomposition into logarithmic-scale spatial blocks.
Implement each block with a constant-order product formula plus a correction to recover exponential accuracy.
Exploit locality so the correction adds no asymptotic depth beyond the block diameter.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an upper bound of O(T log(nT/ε)) depth and O(nT log(nT/ε)) gates, plus an unconditional Ω(log n / log log n) depth lower bound for uniform XXZ Hamiltonians at fixed T and small ε.
watch_item: The result is for time-independent, finite-range Hamiltonians on fixed-dimensional lattices and assumes nearest-neighbor layout, so hardware connectivity or long-range interactions may require different overheads.
paper_title: Toward Optimal Circuit Depth for Geometrically Local Hamiltonian Simulation
